The most serious crime he can be convicted of is **involuntary manslaughter**. His intent to inflict a slight wound (a battery) transfers to the teammate he killed, but that intent does not supply the malice aforethought murder requires. A prosecutor could argue that firing a gun at a person shows depraved-heart malice, which would make it second-degree murder, so the answer is less certain.

CONFIDENCE: 60
